paper_title: Audio-Visual Efficient Conformer for Robust Speech Recognition
caption: Audio-only back-end modules FLOPs (Billion).
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the computational cost, measured in Giga FLOPs (billion floating-point operations), of different modules within the audio-only back-end Conformer architecture across three sequential stages, as described in the paper “Audio-Visual Efficient Conformer for Robust Speech Recognition.” The horizontal axis categorizes the three stages—Stage 1 (d=180, n=500), Stage 2 (d=256, n=250), and Stage 3 (d=360, n=125)—where ‘d’ likely denotes dimensionality and ‘n’ the number of tokens or frames. The vertical axis represents Module Giga FLOPs, scaled from 0 to 0.3 in increments of 0.1. Four module types are compared per stage, color-coded in the legend: blue for “attention,” red for “grouped attention (g=3),” yellow for “patch attention (k=3),” and green for “feed-forward.” In Stage 1, attention has the highest cost at approximately 0.28 Giga FLOPs, followed by grouped attention (~0.15), feed-forward (~0.13), and patch attention (~0.12). In Stage 2, attention remains highest (~0.16), followed by feed-forward (~0.13), grouped attention (~0.12), and patch attention (~0.10). In Stage 3, feed-forward (~0.13) slightly exceeds attention (~0.12), with grouped attention (~0.105) and patch attention (~0.10) being lowest. Across all stages, the attention module consistently incurs the highest or near-highest computational cost, while patch attention consistently has the lowest, indicating its efficiency. The feed-forward module’s cost remains relatively stable across stages, while attention and grouped attention costs decrease with stage progression.
